body:
Players can now walk up to a character in your Unity game and talk to them out loud. The new ElevenAgents Unity SDK connects a scene to an ElevenLabs voice agent. It listens through the player's microphone, plays the agent's voice through an AudioSource , and runs the session through the Conversation API.

The same code runs in the Editor, desktop builds, and WebGL, and iOS, Android, and XR are in beta.

## Start a conversation

A session needs the ID of an agent you've created in the ElevenLabs dashboard, which holds the prompt and the voice. In our GettingStarted sample , included with the SDK, a trigger collider around the character opens the session when the player walks in and closes it when they walk out:

StartSessionAsync returns once the connection is open and the audio devices are ready, and it picks the right transport for the build target. EndSession does nothing if the session has already ended.

## What's in the SDK

## Voices that come from the character

By default the agent's voice plays in 2D. Pass your own AudioSource as OutputAudioSource and the voice comes from the character instead.

GetOutputVolume() returns the agent's current level from 0 to 1 on every platform. The sample uses it to make the cube bob while it talks, and it can drive a mouth animation the same way.

## One agent, many characters

Dynamic variables fill placeholders like {{mood}} in the agent's prompt and first message, so each character can send its own values when its session starts. Values can be strings, numbers, or booleans. In the sample, a yellow happy cube and a red angry cube share one agent:

For bigger changes, Overrides replace part of the agent's configuration for one session, such as the first message or the voice. Each override has to be turned on in the agent's Security settings first.

## Characters that know what's happening

SendContextualUpdate tells the agent about game events mid-conversation, without interrupting it or adding a turn the player didn't say:

## Characters that act in the game

Client tools let the agent trigger game code. Define the tool in the agent's settings, then register a handler under the same name:

The SDK deserializes the tool's parameters with Newtonsoft Json and sends whatever the handler returns back to the agent. Handlers can return an Awaitable for work that takes time, and throw a ClientToolException to tell the agent why something failed.

## Events and controls

Events such as UserTranscriptReceived , AgentResponded , ModeChanged , and Interrupted fire on Unity's main thread, so you can update UI straight from them. Methods cover text input with SendUserMessage , muting with SetMicMuted , SetVolume , frequency data for visualizers, and switching input or output devices mid-session. The Unity SDK docs list them all.

## Platform support

The SDK picks the transport for each target.

• iOS and Android: request microphone permission before you start a session.

• WebGL: turn on Use WebAssembly.Table in Publishing Settings . The SDK fails the build with instructions if it's off. Play Mode doesn't work while WebGL is the active build target, so test on a desktop target.

• WebGL audio: the voice plays through the Web Audio API, so some AudioSource settings, like mixer routing and doppler, don't carry over. WebRTC sessions ignore OutputAudioSource .

The compatibility notes have the full list.

## Get started

• Create an agent in the ElevenLabs dashboard. For a first test, turn off Authentication in its Security settings, so the game can connect with the agent ID alone.

• In Unity, open Window > Package Manager > + > Install package from git URL , and pin the release: https://github.com/elevenlabs/unity.git#v0.1.0

• Import the GettingStarted sample, paste in your agent ID, and press Play.

Warning: Before you ship, turn Authentication back on. Your own server then requests a short-lived signed URL , and the game passes it as SignedUrl instead of AgentId . Never put your ElevenLabs API key in a game build.

The getting started walkthrough takes about 10 minutes and ends with a cube that greets you when you walk up. For everything else, read the Unity SDK docs , and send bugs and feature requests to GitHub issues .

Tadas is a Developer Relations Engineer helping developers build with ElevenLabs product suite. Before he was a founder of a developer education platform, a Lead Developer Advocate at Agora, an instructor at Zero To Mastery, and built an audience on YouTube teaching developers.
ar_body:
أطلقت ElevenLabs حزمة تطوير ElevenAgents Unity SDK التي تتيح للاعبين التحدث بصوتهم مع الشخصيات داخل ألعاب Unity. تربط الحزمة المشهد بوكيل صوتي من ElevenLabs، فتستمع عبر ميكروفون اللاعب وتشغّل صوت الوكيل عبر AudioSource وتدير الجلسة من خلال Conversation API.

• يعمل الكود نفسه في المحرر وإصدارات سطح المكتب وWebGL، بينما يتوفر دعم iOS وAndroid وXR بنسخة تجريبية.
• تحتاج الجلسة إلى معرّف وكيل أُنشئ في لوحة تحكم ElevenLabs يحتوي على التعليمات والصوت.
• يمكن تشغيل صوت الوكيل من الشخصية نفسها بتمرير AudioSource مخصص، كما تتيح الدالة GetOutputVolume() تحريك الفم أو الشخصية أثناء الكلام.
• تتيح المتغيرات الديناميكية استخدام وكيل واحد لعدة شخصيات بقيم مختلفة، مثل المزاج.
• تتيح SendContextualUpdate إبلاغ الوكيل بأحداث اللعبة دون مقاطعته، وتسمح أدوات العميل (Client tools) للوكيل بتشغيل أكواد داخل اللعبة.

تفتح الحزمة الباب أمام شخصيات ألعاب أكثر تفاعلاً وواقعية للمطورين.
